In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the functional strains induced in the radius and the tibia of horses and dogs are constant in magnitude and direction throughout the stance phase of locomotion, and that they increase linearly with the speed of locomotion.

the peak strains are remarkably uniform in wide range of animals, which suggests that the skeleton provides constant safety margins between the peak functional strains and the strain at which failure occurs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional strain magnitudes in the radius and the tibia are constant for a given animal, and the strain rates increase with speed.
the peak strains in the radius of horses and dogs are remarkably similar.
the strains in the limb bones are remarkably constant in both magnitude and orientation, and the magnitude of strain is related to speed of locomotion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peak strains induced during strenuous activity are remarkably uniform across the animal kingdom.

the magnitude of the strains induced during locomotion in the limb bones of the horse are remarkably similar to the strains induced during the same locomotor behaviors in the limb bones in dogs, despite the large differences in body mass between these two species.
bone strains in horses and dogs are not significantly altered by changes in speed or gait, suggesting that these animals have a very high safety margin against bone fracture.
